title: Container Bookings: Dangerous-Goods Bookings and the Late Shipping-Instruction Allowance
content:
Whether a Container Bookings booking may use the free allowance for late shipping instructions depends, for hazardous cargo, on the line's dangerous-goods acceptances.

## Rule

Any booking whose cargo category is something other than dangerous goods has the free allowance open. A booking whose cargo category is dangerous goods has it open only if at least one of its dangerous-goods acceptances stands approved with a container count above zero. The reasoning is that paperwork for hazardous goods still lacking the line's clearance does not count as routine lateness.

## Decision table

| Cargo category on the booking | Dangerous-goods acceptances | Allowance open? |
|---|---|---|
| general, reefer or out of gauge | not relevant | yes |
| dangerous goods | one approved, covering 2 containers | yes |
| dangerous goods | only acceptances under review or rejected | no |
| dangerous goods | none at all | no |

## Evidence

The cargo category is taken from the booking record; acceptance status and container counts come from the dangerous-goods acceptance records linked to the booking. The cases shown are hypothetical.
